steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes differ significantly between treated (n=5) and control (n=5) muscle samples, and how sensitive is that gene list to the inclusion of sample_03?

grounding.reason: DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm shrinkage per R-0001/R-0009; outlier sample with only 5 replicates in the smallest group is kept in the primary fit per R-0034/R-0067, with a mandatory sensitivity refit reported per R-0090.

steps.description: Pre-filter genes to those with >=10 counts in >=5 samples (the smallest group size). Build DESeqDataSetFromMatrix with design ~condition, set condition reference level explicitly to 'control', and run the Wald test. Because the smallest group holds only 5 replicates (fewer than the 3-or-more threshold where down-weighting is recommended but the environment lacks a straightforward down-weighting path for DESeq2 alone), fit the model twice: (1) PRIMARY: all 10 samples, keeping sample_03 unless T1S1 established a clear stated technical cause for removal; (2) SENSITIVITY: identical pipeline with sample_03 excluded (4 vs 5). Apply apeglm shrinkage to the treated-vs-control log2 fold change coefficient in both fits. Extract results with BH-adjusted p-values (independent filtering on, alpha=0.05). Report the count of significant genes (padj<0.05) in each fit, the size of the intersection, and the genes that change significance status between fits. Inspect and report the p-value histogram shape for both fits before trusting the adjusted p-values. Produce MA plots and dispersion plots for both fits.
acceptance_criteria: Pre-filter applied: gene kept only if >=10 counts in >=5 samples
Two DESeq2 Wald-test fits produced: primary (n=10) and sensitivity (sample_03 excluded, n=9)

Number of significant genes (padj<0.05), the intersection size, and genes changing status between the two fits are explicitly reported

steps.description: Take the significant gene list (padj<0.05) from the PRIMARY DESeq2 fit (T1S2, all 10 samples) as the query set, and the full list of genes that passed the low-count filter and were tested by DESeq2 as the explicit universe. Run over-representation analysis (e.g. clusterProfiler::enricher) against three human gene-set collections in sequence, each reported separately (never merged into one set list): (1) MSigDB Hallmark (50 sets), (2) Reactome pathways (filtered to Homo sapiens via the Reactome pathway index), (3) WikiPathways human collection. Apply a gene-set size window of 15-500 members (post-intersection with the universe) for each collection. Adjust p-values within each collection with BH. If the significant gene list has fewer than ~50 genes, state this explicitly in the output alongside the caveat that ORA on a short list has low power, and report the ORA result as exploratory. Collapse redundant/overlapping significant gene sets before final reporting, keeping the full table as supplement.

Universe explicitly set to the DESeq2-tested gene set, not the whole genome
Gene set size window of 15-500 applied per collection
BH-adjusted p-values reported per collection
If <50 significant genes entered the analysis, this is stated explicitly as a power caveat
Redundant overlapping sets collapsed in the primary report, full table kept as supplement

MA plot and dispersion plot included for each fit
ORA results per collection presented with universe and size window stated
Full reproducibility record (versions, seed if applicable, thresholds, collection releases) included

plan.title: Treated vs control muscle DE with outlier-sensitivity check
plan.analytical_narrative: 12000-gene salmon-quantified counts across 5 treated vs 5 control human muscle samples (single batch, unpaired) go through sample-structure QC first, because sample_03 was flagged as departing from its group on PCA/the sample-distance heatmap — the QC step investigates a technical cause (library size, detected-gene count, mapping metrics) before any decision on it. DESeq2 fits the treated-vs-control contrast twice — once with all 10 samples (primary, since the outlier policy for a group of 5 is to keep and not remove without a stated technical cause) and once excluding sample_03 (sensitivity) — with apeglm shrinkage of the log2 fold change and BH-adjusted Wald tests. Both gene lists are compared explicitly so the reader can judge how much of the result depends on that one sample. The resulting significant gene list feeds an over-representation analysis (ORA, since the enrichment knowledge-check rejected preranked GSEA for this situation) against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways human collections, with the tested genes as the explicit universe. A final report consolidates both DE fits, diagnostics, and the enrichment results with full reproducibility metadata.

steps.method: vst(blind) + PCA + sample distance heatmap + library size/detected-gene diagnostics
Keep gene with >=10 counts in >=5 samples (smallest group size)
DESeqDataSetFromMatrix, explicit reference level = control, contrast treated vs control
DESeq2 Wald test, primary run keeps sample_03 (down-weight not remove per outlier rule), sensitivity run excludes sample_03
apeglm shrinkage of the treated-vs-control coefficient
Benjamini-Hochberg on Wald p-values with independent filtering, alpha=0.05
fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic against MSigDB Hallmark, then Reactome and WikiPathways human collections
Report both fits (with/without sample_03), overlap of DE gene sets, MA plot, dispersion plot, leading-edge genes, session info
fgsea preranked GSEA on DESeq2 Wald statistic (stat column) against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets, then follow-up against Reactome and WikiPathways human collections

Over-representation analysis (clusterProfiler enricher) of the significant genes (padj<0.05) against MSigDB Hallmark gene sets with the tested genes as the explicit universe, followed by Reactome and WikiPathways human collections
